workEn: The Secret History of the Mongols
title: 元朝秘史 §§278–278
titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §278: Ögödei's decree on the guards
source: Mongγol-un niγuča tobčiyan (The Secret History of the Mongols), §§278–278, in the Ming Chinese-character phonetic transcription, as edited with a romanized reading by Shiratori Kurakichi 白鳥庫吉, 音訳蒙文元朝秘史 (Tokyo, 1943), itself based on the Ye Dehui 葉德輝 printed edition of 1905/1908; text taken from the Japanese Wikisource transcription, archived and verified against it character for character. Shiratori died in 1942, so the edition was public domain in Japan before the URAA date and was never restored in the United States. Section numbering (§) is the standard citation system. Romanization convention: Shiratori's, kept exactly as he prints it (γ, ġ, ṅ, ž, č, and the raised dot of γ̇). Translations are made fresh from the Mongolian, with the Ming interlinear Chinese glosses as the primary crib. No modern translation was consulted. langCode is null: there is no text-to-speech for Middle Mongol.
about: Ögödei issues a long decree to regulate his guard, the night guard, day guards and quiver-bearers of Chinggis's time. It sets who lodges where, who may walk where, how the four shifts are staffed, the penalties for missing a shift, and the rank of his guardsmen over officers in the field.
draftNote: The Mongol readings follow Shiratori throughout; the English is a first drafting.

sentences.t: Basa Ögödei Qaγan žarliγ bolurun:

morph.gloss: Ögödei, a man's name (personal name) [(人)名]

sentences.l: Again Ögödei Qaγan decree when-becoming:
sentences.i: Again Ögödei Qahan issued a decree:
sentences.n: Read this section by its endings. Žarliγ bolurun (Ming 聖旨做時) is the formula “when the decree became”, which we render “issued a decree”: bol- “become” + the converb of time -urun. Basa (Ming 再) is “again”. The whole section is Ögödei's decree on the guards: kebteġül (night guard), qorčin (quiver-bearers), turγaγ̇ud (day guards), kešigten (men on a shift). Third-person commands end in -tuγai or -tügei, “let him …”, and I mark each one as it comes.

The list is bare nouns; qorčin is qor “quiver” + -či + -n, and turγaγ̇ud is “day guards” (house rendering). Uncertain which noun min-u modifies.

sentences.l: "Qaγan father-of decree-by formerly how going-ones were.
sentences.i: “By the decree of the Qahan, my father, as they used to go before,
sentences.n: Opening mark is Shiratori's. Žarlig(i)-jar is “by the decree” (Ming 聖旨依着: the instrumental -jar means “following”); ečige-jin is “of the father” (-jin after a vowel). Jabuqun büleġei (Ming 行的每有來) is “those who went, there was”, that is the habit of earlier times. Ker (Ming 怎生) is “how”. Here ečige-jin means Ögödei's father, Chinggis.

sentences.l: others inward ?-forcing entering people-OBJ having-seized night-guard heads their cleaving chopping let-go.
sentences.i: others, people who enter inward by force: the night guard who have seized them are to split and hack their heads, and let it go at that.
sentences.n: Very uncertain. Busud (Ming 別每) “others”; dotoγši “toward the inside”; žöričen (Ming 交慘 “cause misery”) I cannot read and take as “by force, recklessly”. The Ming gives 劈開 and 劈着 for dalbaru and čabčižu (both “cleave”), and 去者 for oγ̇ortuγai, so “let it go” may mean “let it pass”, “let it be so”; I give “let it go at that”. An-u (Ming 他的) stands after ekid, “their heads”, as in-ü follows its noun: the heads are those of the people seized. The grammar is clear (two converbs, then an optative) but the sense of the last word is a guess.

Ümerēče (Ming (北)行) is ümer “behind, back” + the ablative (“from behind”, as in the glossary); the glossators bracket 北 “north”, which would suit the back of a tent, so I put “behind the tent”. sentences.n: Shiratori prints only the closing mark (at bariγdalaγ̇a). This is an inner quotation inside the decree that began at Süni, so in `i` I supply an opening single quote and close it with a single quote. Itegeltü is itegel “trust” + -tü “having”; böġetele (bü- + -tele, “while, although”). Bariγdalaγ̇a is bari- “seize” + passive -γda- + a past ending; “was seized”. Degeġün (Ming 上) “over, across”; žilda (Ming 晩夕 “evening”) I read “in the evening”, as the glossary does.
